content: Colesevelam is a medication prescribed to help reduce cholesterol and certain fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with exercise and dietary changes, such as limiting cholesterol and fat intake. This medication works by binding to bile acids in the intestines. Bile acids are produced when cholesterol is broken down in the body. By removing these bile acids, colesevelam helps lower blood cholesterol levels. High levels of cholesterol and fats can accumulate along the walls of arteries, a condition known as atherosclerosis, which reduces blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart, brain, and other parts of the body. Lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood can help prevent heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Colesevelam can be used alone or in combination with other lipid-lowering medications, such as statins (e.g., atorvastatin, lovastatin, pravastatin, or simvastatin). It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Colesevelam is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once or twice daily with meals and liquids. Your doctor will specify the number of tablets to take per dose. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take colesevelam exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Lipid levels should begin to decrease within two weeks of starting the medication. However, colesevelam does not cure high cholesterol, so you should continue taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking colesevelam without consulting your doctor. Before starting colesevelam, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to colesevelam or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially sustained-release formulations of verapamil (e.g., Calan SR), vitamins, and herbal products. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had gastrointestinal problems, such as bowel obstruction or difficulty swallowing, triglyceride levels greater than 300 mg/dL, bleeding disorders, or low levels of fat-soluble vitamins (A, E, and K). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking colesevelam, contact your doctor immediately. While taking colesevelam, adhere to a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This diet should include foods such as cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as liver, fatty meats, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of colesevelam, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Colesevelam may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: gas, constipation, upset stomach, headache, weakness, muscle pain, or throat infection. Store colesevelam in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests will be ordered to monitor your response to colesevelam. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
